summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived introduction to Haryana, one of the 29 states of India located in North India. It covers the state's creation in 1966 from East Punjab on a linguistic basis, its area rank, its 2011 census population rank, and its key cities. Chandigarh is the capital, Faridabad is the most populous city, and Gurugram is described as the financial hub of the National Capital Region.
one_line: Overview of Haryana, a North Indian state formed in 1966 from East Punjab, with its area, population, and key cities.
key_facts: Haryana is one of the 29 states in India and is situated in North India.
Haryana was carved out of the former state of East Punjab on 1 November 1966 on a linguistic basis.
Haryana stands 21st in terms of its area, which is spread about 44,212 km (17,070 sq mi).
As of the 2011 census of India, Haryana is the eighteenth largest state by population.
Haryana had 25,353,081 inhabitants at the 2011 census of India.
The city of Chandigarh is the capital of Haryana.
The National Capital Region city of Faridabad is the most populous city of Haryana.
The city of Gurugram is the financial hub of the National Capital Region.
Major Fortune 500 companies are located in Gurugram.
The name Haryana is written in Urdu as ہریانہ.
The note gives the IPA pronunciation of Haryana as (ɦərɪˈjaːɳaː).
